what_to_do: Ensure rest, fluids, and monitor breathing closely.
what_to_avoid: Avoid exposure to smoke or pollutants.
diet_recommendation: Adequate fluids and light, nutritious food.
home_care: Keep the child comfortable and monitor breathing rate.
monitoring_advice: Seek care if breathing becomes fast, labored, or the child appears lethargic.

what_to_do: Keep the child safe during the seizure and seek prompt medical evaluation.
what_to_avoid: Avoid restraining the child or putting anything in their mouth during a seizure.
diet_recommendation: Balanced diet; no specific dietary link.
home_care: Manage fever with medication as advised and monitor closely.
monitoring_advice: Discuss seizure recurrence risk and management plan with the pediatrician.

what_to_do: Follow a structured nutritional rehabilitation plan with a health worker.
what_to_avoid: Avoid delaying nutritional intervention.
diet_recommendation: Calorie and protein-dense foods appropriate for age.
home_care: Regular growth monitoring.
monitoring_advice: Track weight and height gain against growth charts over time.

what_to_do: Seek prompt medical care for any complications like breathing difficulty or ear pain.
what_to_avoid: Avoid delaying care if the child appears increasingly unwell.
diet_recommendation: Soft, nutritious food and fluids.
home_care: Monitor closely during the recovery period.
monitoring_advice: Follow up as advised, especially for vision or hearing changes.

what_to_do: Follow the prescribed vitamin D and calcium supplementation plan.
what_to_avoid: Avoid prolonged lack of sun exposure.
diet_recommendation: Calcium and vitamin D-rich foods.
home_care: Encourage safe outdoor time for sun exposure.
monitoring_advice: Follow up growth and bone health as advised.

what_to_do: Moisturize regularly and use prescribed treatments during flares.
what_to_avoid: Avoid known triggers and harsh soaps.
diet_recommendation: Balanced diet; note any specific food triggers if identified.
home_care: Use fragrance-free moisturizers and avoid scratching.
monitoring_advice: Track flare frequency and triggers to discuss with a doctor.

what_to_do: Follow the prescribed treatment plan and moisturize regularly.
what_to_avoid: Avoid known triggers like stress and skin injury.
diet_recommendation: Anti-inflammatory diet.
food_to_limit: Alcohol and processed food, which may worsen flares for some.
home_care: Manage stress, which can trigger flares.
monitoring_advice: Track flare patterns and follow up with a dermatologist.

what_to_do: Follow the treatment plan recommended by a dermatologist.
what_to_avoid: Avoid excessive sun exposure on affected areas without protection.
diet_recommendation: Balanced diet; no proven specific dietary link.
home_care: Use sun protection on depigmented areas.
monitoring_advice: Follow up periodically to monitor patch changes.

what_to_do: Follow up with an ophthalmologist to monitor vision changes.
what_to_avoid: Avoid delaying evaluation if vision significantly affects daily activities.
diet_recommendation: Balanced diet rich in antioxidants.
home_care: Use adequate lighting and avoid night driving if vision is impaired.
monitoring_advice: Follow up regularly to assess if surgery is needed.

what_to_do: Use prescribed eye drops consistently and attend regular checkups.
what_to_avoid: Avoid missing doses, as this can worsen eye pressure control.
diet_recommendation: Balanced diet; no specific dietary link.
food_to_limit: Excess caffeine in large amounts, which may affect eye pressure.
home_care: Protect vision by following the treatment plan closely.
monitoring_advice: Regular eye pressure and vision field monitoring.

what_to_do: Use prescribed corrective glasses or lenses.
what_to_avoid: Avoid prolonged near-work without breaks.
diet_recommendation: Balanced diet; no specific dietary link.
home_care: Follow the 20-20-20 rule during screen use.
monitoring_advice: Periodic eye checkups to update prescription as needed.

what_to_do: Complete prescribed antibiotics if given, and manage pain as advised.
what_to_avoid: Avoid inserting objects into the ear.
diet_recommendation: Balanced diet; no specific dietary link.
home_care: Keep the ear dry during treatment.
monitoring_advice: Follow up if pain persists or hearing seems affected after treatment.

what_to_do: Use prescribed treatment and steam inhalation for relief.
what_to_avoid: Avoid known allergens and irritants.
diet_recommendation: Warm fluids, adequate hydration.
home_care: Steam inhalation and saline nasal rinses may help.
monitoring_advice: Seek care if symptoms persist beyond 10 days or worsen.

what_to_do: Identify and avoid known allergens where possible.
what_to_avoid: Avoid known triggers like dust, pollen, or pet dander.
diet_recommendation: Balanced diet; no specific dietary link.
home_care: Use air purifiers and keep living spaces clean of dust.
monitoring_advice: Track symptom patterns in relation to seasons or exposures.

what_to_do: Rest for 24-48 hours if severe, then resume gentle activity gradually.
what_to_avoid: Avoid heavy lifting and prolonged bed rest beyond 2 days.
diet_recommendation: Balanced diet; no specific dietary link.
home_care: Apply heat or cold as comfortable; maintain good posture and use a firm mattress.
monitoring_advice: Seek care if pain radiates down the leg, or if there is numbness or weakness.

what_to_do: Rest, manage stress, and use over-the-counter pain relief as advised.
what_to_avoid: Avoid excess caffeine and poor posture during screen use.
diet_recommendation: Regular meals; stay hydrated.
home_care: Apply gentle neck and shoulder stretches; take regular screen breaks.
monitoring_advice: Seek care if headaches become frequent, severe, or change in pattern.

what_to_do: Drink plenty of water (2.5 to 3 liters daily) and take prescribed pain relief.
what_to_avoid: Avoid excess sodium, animal protein, and high-oxalate foods without balance.
diet_recommendation: Adequate fluids, fresh lemonade, calcium-rich foods paired with meals.
food_to_limit: Excess salt, spinach, nuts, chocolates, and heavy red meat.
home_care: Filter urine to catch stones for analysis if advised; apply local heat for flank pain.
monitoring_advice: Seek immediate emergency care if severe pain is accompanied by fever or inability to pass urine.

what_to_do: Increase dietary fiber and water intake to keep stools soft.
what_to_avoid: Avoid straining during bowel movements and sitting on the toilet for prolonged periods.
diet_recommendation: High-fiber diet (whole grains, oats, papaya, legumes) and adequate water.
food_to_limit: Spicy, fried, and low-fiber processed foods.
home_care: Take warm sitz baths 2-3 times daily for symptom relief; avoid rough wiping.
monitoring_advice: Monitor for rectal bleeding, and seek clinical review if pain worsens or bleeding is persistent.

what_to_do: Engage in regular physical activity and maintain regular bowel habits.
what_to_avoid: Avoid ignoring the urge to pass stool and over-relying on stimulant laxatives.
diet_recommendation: High-fiber fruits (prunes, figs, apples), vegetables, and warm fluids.
food_to_limit: Processed flour (maida), fast food, and excess dairy.
home_care: Drink warm water first thing in the morning; practice abdominal massage.
monitoring_advice: Track bowel movements; seek care if constipation lasts over 2 weeks or is paired with unexplained weight loss.

what_to_do: Use prescribed stool softeners and topical healing ointments.
what_to_avoid: Avoid passing hard stools and aggressive wiping.
diet_recommendation: High-fiber soft diet with abundant water intake.
home_care: Take warm sitz baths after bowel movements to relax the anal sphincter.
monitoring_advice: Monitor bleeding during defecation; seek surgical or medical evaluation if healing stalls.

what_to_do: Eat smaller and balanced low-fat meals; follow surgeon guidance.
what_to_avoid: Avoid crash dieting and skipping meals which worsen gallbladder stasis.
diet_recommendation: Fiber-rich foods, oats, vegetables, and lean proteins.
food_to_limit: Fried items, creamy gravies, full-fat dairy, and trans fats.
home_care: Maintain a healthy weight through gradual weight loss.
monitoring_advice: Seek emergency care if severe right upper quadrant pain radiates to the shoulder with fever or jaundice.

what_to_do: Follow a strict lifelong 100% gluten-free diet.
what_to_avoid: Avoid even trace amounts of wheat, rye, barley, and contaminated oats.
diet_recommendation: Naturally gluten-free grains (rice, millets, quinoa, corn) and fresh produce.
food_to_limit: Wheat, maida, sooji, hing (compounded with wheat), and processed gravies.
home_care: Check food labels diligently and use separate cookware to prevent cross-contamination.
monitoring_advice: Monitor antibody levels (anti-tTG) and nutrient absorption (iron, calcium) annually.

what_to_do: Switch to plant-based milk or lactose-free dairy alternatives.
what_to_avoid: Avoid consuming large quantities of milk or fresh cream directly.
diet_recommendation: Lactose-free milk, fortified almond/soy milk, hard aged cheeses, and yogurt.
food_to_limit: Cow's milk, ice cream, paneer in large quantities, and soft cheeses.
home_care: Use lactase enzyme drops/tablets if consuming dairy; introduce fermented dairy gradually.
monitoring_advice: Ensure adequate calcium and vitamin D intake from non-dairy or fortified sources.

what_to_do: Maintain daily posture exercises and take prescribed anti-inflammatory therapy.
what_to_avoid: Avoid smoking and prolonged static sitting or stooping.
diet_recommendation: Anti-inflammatory diet rich in omega-3 and antioxidants.
food_to_limit: Excess processed foods, refined sugars, and inflammatory fats.
home_care: Sleep on a firm mattress with minimal pillow support; practice daily spinal stretches.
monitoring_advice: Track spinal mobility, chest expansion, and morning stiffness duration with a rheumatologist.

what_to_do: Wear a wrist splint at night and take frequent ergonomic breaks.
what_to_avoid: Avoid repetitive wrist flexion, heavy gripping, and awkward wrist postures.
diet_recommendation: Balanced diet; vitamin B6-rich foods under guidance.
food_to_limit: Excess sodium which may promote fluid retention.
home_care: Apply cold packs during flare-ups; adjust keyboard and workstation ergonomics.
monitoring_advice: Seek medical review if there is progressive thumb weakness, numbness, or loss of hand grip.

what_to_do: Perform calf and plantar fascia stretching exercises daily.
what_to_avoid: Avoid walking barefoot on hard floors and wearing worn-out, unsupportive footwear.
diet_recommendation: Balanced nutrient-dense diet to assist weight management.
food_to_limit: No specific restriction beyond maintaining healthy weight.
home_care: Use supportive orthotic footwear with cushioned heels; roll a frozen water bottle under the foot.
monitoring_advice: Monitor first-step morning heel pain; consult an orthopedist if pain persists beyond 6 weeks.

what_to_do: Protect the affected eye with lubricating drops and eye patches; take prescribed steroids promptly.
what_to_avoid: Avoid exposing the affected facial side to direct cold drafts.
diet_recommendation: Soft, easy-to-chew foods to prevent cheek biting.
food_to_limit: Hard or chewy foods during active paralysis.
home_care: Perform gentle facial massage and facial muscle exercises as function returns.
monitoring_advice: Monitor eye closure and cornea hydration; review with a neurologist for recovery progress.

what_to_do: Perform repositioning maneuvers (such as Epley maneuver) under clinical guidance.
what_to_avoid: Avoid sudden head movements, looking upward rapidly, or bending forward quickly.
diet_recommendation: Stay well-hydrated; balanced light meals.
home_care: Keep rooms well lit; install grab bars and move slowly when getting out of bed.
monitoring_advice: Seek immediate care if vertigo is accompanied by double vision, speech difficulty, or weakness.

what_to_do: Use preservative-free artificial tears and follow the 20-20-20 screen rule.
what_to_avoid: Avoid direct air vents blowing on eyes, smoky environments, and prolonged unblinked screen time.
diet_recommendation: Omega-3 fatty acid rich foods (flaxseeds, walnuts, chia seeds).
home_care: Use a room humidifier and apply warm compresses to eyelids daily.
monitoring_advice: Follow up with an eye specialist if redness, severe gritty pain, or vision blurriness develops.

what_to_do: Practice strict daily eyelid hygiene using warm diluted baby shampoo or lid scrubs.
what_to_avoid: Avoid eye makeup and wearing contact lenses during active inflammation.
diet_recommendation: Balanced anti-inflammatory diet.
home_care: Apply warm compresses to closed eyes for 5-10 minutes twice daily to loosen secretions.
monitoring_advice: Monitor for stye formation, corneal irritation, or spreading redness to the eye.

what_to_do: Cleanse face gently twice daily with a mild foaming wash and use prescribed topical treatments.
what_to_avoid: Avoid picking, popping, or squeezing pimples, and avoid harsh abrasive scrubs.
diet_recommendation: Low glycemic index foods, abundant water, and fresh vegetables.
food_to_limit: High glycemic foods, excessive sugary drinks, and skim milk/whey protein supplements.
home_care: Use non-comedogenic sunscreen and moisturizers; change pillowcases regularly.
monitoring_advice: Monitor skin barrier health; consult a dermatologist if painful cystic lesions or scarring occur.

what_to_do: Identify and avoid known physical or allergen triggers; take prescribed antihistamines.
what_to_avoid: Avoid hot baths, tight-fitting clothes, alcohol, and unverified NSAIDs.
diet_recommendation: Fresh whole foods; low-histamine diet if specific sensitivity exists.
food_to_limit: Alcohol, aged cheeses, shellfish, or suspected allergen-heavy foods.
home_care: Apply cool compresses and calamine lotion to soothe itching skin.
monitoring_advice: Seek emergency medical attention immediately if swelling involves lips, tongue, throat, or breathing.

what_to_do: Identify and discontinue exposure to the offending irritant or chemical allergen.
what_to_avoid: Avoid scratching the rash or applying strong unverified perfumed creams.
diet_recommendation: Balanced diet; adequate hydration.
home_care: Wash exposed skin immediately with mild soap and water; apply cool wet compresses.
monitoring_advice: Follow up if rash covers large body areas, blisters blister heavily, or signs of secondary infection appear.

what_to_do: Undergo therapeutic phlebotomy as scheduled and monitor ferritin levels.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking iron or vitamin C supplements, raw seafood, and alcohol.
diet_recommendation: Balanced diet without iron-fortified cereals or excessive red meat.
food_to_limit: Iron-rich red meats, organ meats, alcohol, and vitamin C supplements with meals.
home_care: Maintain a health log of phlebotomy sessions and energy levels.
monitoring_advice: Regularly test serum ferritin and transferrin saturation to guide therapy.

what_to_do: Wear graduated compression stockings and elevate legs above heart level when resting.
what_to_avoid: Avoid prolonged standing or sitting, crossing legs, and wearing tight waistbands.
diet_recommendation: High-fiber diet to prevent constipation, low-sodium meals to reduce leg edema.
home_care: Engage in daily walking and ankle pump exercises to promote venous return.
monitoring_advice: Seek medical attention if leg skin becomes hardened, discolored, or forms open ulcers.

what_to_do: Manage underlying blood sugars diligently and inspect feet daily for injuries.
what_to_avoid: Avoid walking barefoot, smoking, and wearing tight or ill-fitting shoes.
diet_recommendation: Vitamin B12 and folate-rich foods, antioxidant-rich fruits and vegetables.
home_care: Keep feet clean, moisturized (except between toes), and use cushioned socks.
monitoring_advice: Schedule regular diabetic foot screenings and sensory evaluations with a clinician.

what_to_do: Rest the bowel, drink oral rehydration salts (ORS), and reintroduce bland food slowly.
what_to_avoid: Avoid dairy, spicy dishes, caffeine, and over-the-counter anti-motility drugs unless prescribed.
diet_recommendation: Dilute broths, rice water, khichdi, banana, and ORS.
food_to_limit: Oily dishes, dairy products, carbonated beverages, and raw vegetables.
home_care: Wash hands thoroughly with soap; sanitize shared surfaces and isolate utensils.
monitoring_advice: Seek hospital care if vomiting prevents fluid retention or if signs of severe dehydration develop.

what_to_do: Perform gentle pendulum and passive stretching exercises within pain-free limits.
what_to_avoid: Avoid sudden aggressive jerking of the arm and completely immobilizing the shoulder.
diet_recommendation: Anti-inflammatory diet rich in antioxidants.
food_to_limit: Excess refined sugar and processed foods.
home_care: Apply moist heat before stretching exercises and cold packs post-exercise.
monitoring_advice: Track passive range of motion with a physiotherapist; consult an orthopedist for persistent stiffness.

what_to_do: Use antiseptic/anesthetic oral gels and maintain gentle oral hygiene.
what_to_avoid: Avoid very hot, spicy, salty, or sharp hard-textured foods.
diet_recommendation: Soft, cool foods like curd, fruit smoothies, and mild soups.
food_to_limit: Spicy chilies, citrus fruits, pineapple, and salty potato chips.
home_care: Rinse mouth with salt water; use a soft-bristle toothbrush.
monitoring_advice: Consult a doctor if ulcers exceed 1 cm, persist past 2 weeks, or cause severe difficulty eating.

what_to_do: Stay well-hydrated, rest the voice, and use warm saline gargles.
what_to_avoid: Avoid smoking, exposure to secondhand smoke, dust, and shouting/voice strain.
diet_recommendation: Warm herbal teas with honey, warm broths, and soft foods.
food_to_limit: Very cold drinks, excessively sour foods, and throat irritants.
home_care: Use a cool mist bedroom humidifier; avoid mouth breathing where possible.
monitoring_advice: Seek evaluation if sore throat is accompanied by high fever, difficulty swallowing, or neck swelling.
